On its boundary, the 0-form symmetry acts by stacking with a 2+1d linear SSPT phase, signaling a mixed 't Hooft anomaly.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Furukawa, Takuya Okuda

item.title: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
item.description: arXiv:2611.17245v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure $N$-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation. To resolve scaling bottlenecks of explicit two-body cumulant methods, we project the two-body cumulant onto its lowest unitary invariant and evaluate a susceptibility-windowed orbital scattering scale via a single Coulomb-exchange contraction. Relaxing onto a hyperbolic-tangent cumulant attractor through Markovian collisional relaxation yields a parameter-free Quantum Boltzmann Equation Cumulant-Kernel that regularizes derivative cusps without thermal smearing. Using the collinear $\mathrm{H}_3$ exchange reaction, the symmetric $D_{4h}$ square $\mathrm{H}_4$ dissociation, the non-adiabatic avoided crossing in $\mathrm{BeH}_2$, the symmetric bond cleavage of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the triple-bond dissociation of $\mathrm{N}_2$, the 11-molecule MR-MGN-BE17 dissociation test set, and the singlet diradical isomers of benzyne as case studies, we show that this kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.
item.dc:creator: Romit Chakraborty

item.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
item.description: arXiv:2611.17306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.
item.dc:creator: Bibek Saha, David E. Logan, Sthitadhi Roy

item.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
item.description: arXiv:2611.17333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.
item.dc:creator: Anirban Das, Asmi Haldar, Arnab Das

item.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
item.description: arXiv:2611.17335v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.
item.dc:creator: Xian P. Yang, Christopher T. Parzyck, Martin Cross, Ella Blake, Octave Duros, Yinchuan Lv, Hari Paudyal, Che-Min Lin, Sharon S. Philip, Lingjia Shen, Daniel Jost, Giacomo Coslovich, Joshua J. Turner, Choongwon Seo, Elyse Schriber, Michael E. Flatt\'e, Xiaoqin Li, Yuri Suzuki, Durga Paudyal, Harold Y. Hwang, Georgi L. Dakovski, Matthias C. Hoffmann, Wei-Sheng Lee, Alexander H. Reid

item.title: Quantum Measurements and Conservation Laws
item.description: arXiv:2108.08342v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When a measurement is made on a system that is not in an eigenstate of the measured observable, it is often assumed that some conservation law has been violated. But this assumption results from ignoring the entanglement between the measured system and the preparation apparatus. The preparation of a system in any particular state necessarily involves interaction between the apparatus and the system, and this interaction generates entanglement. The amount of entanglement is very small, but the apparatus typically has an enormous number of degrees of freedom; this implies that a very tiny difference between the apparatus states that are correlated with the orthogonal states of the measured system can be sufficient to account for the perceived deviation from strict conservation of the quantity in question. After reviewing entanglement relations for a typical measurement situation with a macroscopic preparation apparatus I identify microscopic processes involving analogous entanglement relations in which measurements on both entangled systems demonstrate exact conservation of the relevant quantities. The close analogy strongly suggests that conservation laws hold exactly in all measurement processes.
item.dc:creator: Edward J. Gillis

item.title: Factorization, partner Hamiltonians and intelligent states in $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric position dependent effective mass systems
item.description: arXiv:2208.10336v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a factorized $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric position-dependent mass Hamiltonian on a finite interval with quasiperiodic boundary conditions. A positive, bounded, and boundedly invertible metric is constructed explicitly, and the Hamiltonian is shown to be self-adjoint in the associated metric Hilbert space and similar to a Hermitian position-dependent-mass operator. Consequently, its spectrum is real within the stated parameter domain. The reverse factorization defines a $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$-symmetric partner Hamiltonian, and the first-order factors act as intertwining operators. Eigenstates of the lowering-type factorization operator are consequently interpreted as Robertson intelligent states, not as states generated by an energy ladder. Their admissible eigenvalues are quantized by the quasiperiodic boundary condition, and they saturate the corresponding Robertson-Schr\"{o}dinger uncertainty relation. A weakly position-dependent mass profile illustrates the construction within the explicitly quantified regime.
item.dc:creator: Pinaki Patra

item.title: Quantum randomness certification with untrusted measurements and few probe states
item.description: arXiv:2210.13608v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a scheme for semidevice-independent quantum randomness certification from an untrusted measurement device and a trusted source and demonstrate it experimentally. No assumptions about noise or imperfections in the measurement are required, and the scheme is simple to implement with existing technology. The measurement device is probed with a few trusted states, and the output entropy can be lower bounded conditioned on the observed outcome distribution. The protocol can be applied to measurements with any finite number of outcomes and, in particular, can be realized by homodyne measurements of the vacuum using a detector probed by coherent states, as we experimentally demonstrate by intensity modulation of a telecom-wavelength pilot laser followed by homodyne detection and discretization by analog-to-digital conversion. We show that randomness can be certified in the presence of both Gaussian additive noise and non-Gaussian imperfections.
item.dc:creator: Makoto Ishihara, Carles Roch i Carceller, Kieran Neil Wilkinson, Casper Ahl Breum, Tobias Gehring, Jonatan Bohr Brask

item.title: Local entanglement of electrons in 1D hydrogen molecule
item.description: arXiv:2308.01708v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quantum entanglement entropy of the electrons in one-dimensional hydrogen molecule is quantified locally using an appropriate partitioning of the two-dimensional configuration space. Both the global and the local entanglement entropy exhibit a monotonic increase when increasing the inter-nuclear distance, while the local entropy remains peaked at the middle between the nuclei with its width decreasing. Our findings show that at the inter-nuclear distance where stable hydrogen molecule is formed, the quantum entropy shows no peculiarity thus indicating that the entropy and the energy measures display different sensitivity with respect to the interaction between the two identical electrons involved. One possible explanation is that the calculation of the quantum entropy does not account explicitly for the distance between the nuclei, which contrasts to the total energy calculation where the energy minimum depends decisively on that distance. The numerically exact and the time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo calculations show close results.
item.dc:creator: Ivan P. Christov

item.title: Approximate recoverability and the quantum data processing inequality
item.description: arXiv:2309.02074v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we discuss the quantum data processing inequality and its refinements that are physically meaningful in the context of approximate recoverability. An important conjecture regarding this due to Seshadreesan et. al. in J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 48 (2015) is disproved. We prove some inequalities capturing universal approximate recoverability with the Petz recovery map for the sandwiched quasi and R\'enyi relative entropies for the parameter $t=2$. We also obtain convexity theorems on some parametrized versions of the relative entropy and fidelity, which can be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Saptak Bhattacharya

item.title: A Jordan Algebraic Approach to the Landau Problem with a Non-commutative Parameter: From Non-commutativity to Non-associativity
item.description: arXiv:2312.12047v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Non-associative structures arise naturally in several areas of fundamental physics, including the quantum mechanics of charged particles in magnetic monopole backgrounds, or non-geometric flux compactifications in string theory. A key observation motivating the present work is that the non-commutativity of spatial coordinates can be recast as the non-associativity of observables within a Jordan algebraic framework. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the Jordan algebraic, non-associative formulation of quantum mechanics and demonstrates this passage from non-commutativity to non-associativity concretely through the non-commutative Landau problem coupled to a harmonic potential. We begin with a self-contained account of the operator algebra background, covering $C^*$-algebras, von Neumann algebras, and Jordan--Banach ($JB$) and Jordan--von Neumann ($JBW$) algebras, and present the axiomatic formulation of quantum mechanics in terms of the Jordan algebra of observables. We then develop an alternative Hilbert space construction based on 3-cyclic traces, extending the work of Schupp and Szabo to infinite dimensional Jordan algebras. A central result of this work is that the non-commutative parameter $\theta$ can be expressed entirely in terms of an associator in the Jordan algebraic setting. Pure product states and density matrices arising from this construction are characterized within the JBW-algebra framework. A key advantage of our approach is the \emph{explicit} construction of split operators for the non-commutative Landau Hamiltonian, turning an abstract existence result into a concrete decomposition. This leads to the Jordan--Schr\"odinger time-evolution equation for state vectors, whose exact closed-form solution is presented.
item.dc:creator: Tekin Dereli, Ekin S{\i}la Y\"or\"uk

item.title: Detecting quantum properties in physical systems using proxy witnesses
item.description: arXiv:2407.12933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In practice, it is quite challenging to detect a quantum property, a microscopic property, in a system. In our work, we construct general proxy witnesses of quantum properties to detect their presence in quantum systems and we do so for quantum systems which may possibly be large. In particular, we discuss proxy witnesses for quantum properties like unextendibility, quantum coherence, activation, steerability, and entanglement. We apply these proxy witnesses in some widely considered examples of many-body systems, viz., the quantum Heisenberg models and the quantum J1-J2 model.
item.dc:creator: Priya Ghosh, Ujjwal Sen, Siddhartha Das

item.title: Symmetries, correlation functions, and entanglement of general quantum Motzkin spin-chains
item.description: arXiv:2408.16070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motzkin spin-chains, which include `colorless' (integer spin $s=1$) and `colorful' ($s \geq 2$) variants, are one-dimensional (1D) local integer spin models notable for their lack of a conformal field theory (CFT) description of their low-energy physics, despite being gapless. The colorful variants are particularly unusual, as they exhibit power-law violation of the area-law of entanglement entropy (as $\sqrt{n}$ in system size $n$), rather than a logarithmic violation as seen in a CFT. In this work, we analytically discover several unique properties of these models, potentially suggesting a new universality class for their low-energy physics. We identify a complex structure of symmetries and unexpected scaling behavior in spin-spin correlations, which deviate from known 1D universality classes. Specifically, the $s=1$ chain exhibits $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking and ferromagnetic order. Meanwhile, the $s \geq 2$ chains do not appear to spontaneously break any symmetries, but display quasi-long-range algebraic order with power-law decaying correlations, inconsistent with standard Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) critical exponents. We also derive asymptotic scaling expressions, with explicit additive constants, for entanglement measures in both colorless and colorful chains, generalizing previous results of Movassagh [J. Math Phys. (2017)], while providing benchmarks for potential quantum simulation experiments. The $\sqrt{n}$ entanglement scaling implies that any matrix-product-state description of these ground states requires bond dimension $e^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$; this superpolynomial cost of the standard 1D tensor-network toolkit, along with the analytical tractability of their ground state properties, positions Motzkin spin chains as intriguing testbeds for quantum simulation of many-body physics.
item.dc:creator: Varun Menon, Andi Gu, Ramis Movassagh

item.title: Experimental causal inference from measurements alone in the presence of spatial and temporal quantum correlations
item.description: arXiv:2411.06051v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The causal structure of a set of events specifies which events influence which others. Determining this structure, known as causal inference, is a fundamental task in science. Reset-style intervention is commonly used to determine causal structure in classical scenarios. However, in the more fundamental quantum theory, there is evidence that projective measurements alone can suffice in some cases. We here extend those cases to two systems at two times, more general channels, and from fine-grained to less invasive coarse-grained projective measurements. The measurements are implemented by scattering circuits in a nuclear magnetic resonance platform. The measurement data is analyzed via the pseudo-density matrix (PDM) formalism for measurements on systems at several times, in order to determine compatibility with given causal structures. We thereby successfully demonstrate causal inference from coarse-grained measurements alone, in a scenario with several qubits and two times.
item.dc:creator: Hongfeng Liu, Xiangjing Liu, Qian Chen, Yixian Qiu, Vlatko Vedral, Xinfang Nie, Oscar Dahlsten, Dawei Lu

item.title: High-frequency dispersive readout of a superconducting qubit
item.description: arXiv:2501.09161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Driving a low-dissipation, non-linear system periodically can destabilize it by exciting indirect resonances, which occur whenever an integer multiple of the drive frequency matches an integer combination of the system's mode frequencies. Avoiding such resonances is a central design constraint across physics and engineering, from radio-frequency ion traps to particle accelerators. Remarkably, the measurement of quantum bits based on superconducting circuits has so far remained limited by non-linear resonances. Measurements of qubit states are customarily performed in a regime where the frequency of the microwave readout tone is comparable to that of the circuit. In that case, the drive excites resonances that eject the qubit from its computational subspace. This limits the readout power and hence the achievable measurement fidelity. We show that a readout tone with frequency much larger than that of the circuit circumvents this problem by exponentially suppressing the resonances. Using a readout tone with frequency 12 times larger than that of our transmon qubit, we achieve a quantum non-demolition measurement fidelity of $99.931\pm0.003\%$, with an error an order of magnitude smaller than the previous record. Under these conditions, the probability of leakage to non-computational states per readout is $0.018\pm0.002\%$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel D. Kurilovich, Thomas Connolly, Charlotte G. L. B{\o}ttcher, Daniel K. Weiss, Sumeru Hazra, Vidul R. Joshi, Andy Z. Ding, Heekun Nho, Spencer Diamond, Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Mykola Kishmar, Wei Dai, Valla Fatemi, Luigi Frunzio, Leonid I. Glazman, Michel H. Devoret

item.title: Polarization properties of photon Bose-Einstein condensates
item.description: arXiv:2506.06141v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The first experimental realization of a photon Bose-Einstein condensate was demonstrated more than a decade ago. However, the polarization of the condensate has not been fully understood and measured in this weakly driven-dissipative system. In this letter, we experimentally investigate the polarization of thermal and condensed light depending on the power and polarization of the pump beam. With full control over the polarization of the pump, it is possible to create arbitrary states on the surface of the Poincar\'e sphere. We show that, in agreement with previous theoretical work, there is a remarkable increase in the polarization strength of the condensate above the threshold for a fully linearly polarized pump. Above a certain threshold also the degenerate orthogonal polarized state of the cavity is occupied, limiting the degree of polarization to approximately 90%.
item.dc:creator: Sven Enns, Julian Schulz, Kirankumar Karkihalli Umesh, Frank Vewinger, Georg von Freymann

item.title: Spectral phase encoding for selective atomic excitation in quantum networks
item.description: arXiv:2506.17482v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spectral phase encoding offers a means of distinguishing photons addressed to different quantumnetwork nodes within a shared optical bandwidth. We investigate how this encoding controls the excitation of two-level atomic receivers by single-photon wave packets. Using the Heisenberg-Langevin formalism, we relate atomic excitation to the temporal-mode overlap between the incident photon and the time-reversed spontaneous-emission mode. Matched spectral decoding restores the original photon mode and its excitation response, whereas mismatched codes alter the interference between spectral contributions and can suppress unwanted excitation. We derive the mean cross-talk for independently assigned random binary codes, accounting for the frequency-dependent atomic response. When the spectral contributions have comparable amplitudes and phases, longer codes improve discrimination between intended and unintended photons. We further determine how random spectral-phase errors modify the time-dependent atomic response and limit decoding fidelity. These results connect spectral encoding and decoding to atomic-node addressability and establish conditions for suppressing cross-talk in multiuser quantum networks.
item.dc:creator: Hamid Reza Naeij

item.title: Probing chiral topological order of the Kitaev honeycomb on a trapped ion processor
item.description: arXiv:2507.08939v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Kitaev's honeycomb model is a paradigmatic exactly solvable system hosting a quantum spin liquid with non-Abelian anyons and topologically protected edge modes, offering a platform for fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, real candidate Kitaev materials invariably include complex secondary interactions that obscure the realization of spin-liquid behavior and demand novel quantum computational approaches for efficient simulation. Here we report quantum simulations of a 22-site Kitaev honeycomb lattice on a trapped-ion quantum processor, without and with non-integrable Heisenberg interactions that are present in real materials. We develop efficient quantum circuits for ground-state preparation, achieving high accuracy with energy errors equivalent to an effective temperature $\approx 0.2$ (in units of the Kitaev interactions), consistent with the experimentally relevant spin-liquid regime. Starting from these states, we apply controlled perturbations and measure time-dependent spin correlations along the system's edge. In the non-Abelian phase, we observe chiral edge dynamics consistent with a non-zero Chern number, a hallmark of chiral topological order, which vanishes upon transition to the Abelian toric code phase. Extending to the non-integrable Kitaev-Heisenberg model, we find that weak Heisenberg interactions preserve chiral edge dynamics, while stronger couplings suppress them, signaling the breakdown of topological protection. These simulations establish edge-mode dynamical simulations on quantum computers as a staple technique to understand the topological and chiral phases of matter in Hamiltonians beyond integrability.
item.dc:creator: Ammar Ali, Joe Gibbs, Keerthi Kumaran, Varadharajan Muruganandam, Bo Xiao, Paul Kairys, G\'abor Hal\'asz, Arnab Banerjee, Phillip C. Lotshaw

item.title: Optimal Calibration of Qubit Detuning and Crosstalk
item.description: arXiv:2507.10661v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Characterizing and calibrating physical qubits is essential for maintaining the performance of quantum processors. A key challenge in this process is the presence of crosstalk that complicates the estimation of individual qubit detunings. In this work, we derive optimal strategies for estimating detuning and crosstalk parameters by optimizing Ramsey interference experiments using Fisher information and the Cramer-Rao bound. We compare several calibration protocols, including measurements of a single quadrature at multiple times and of two quadratures at a single time, for a fixed number of total measurements. Our results predict that the latter approach yields the highest precision and robustness in both cases of isolated and coupled qubits. We validate experimentally our approach using a single NV center as well as superconducting transmons. Our approach enables accurate parameter extraction with significantly fewer measurements, resulting in up to a 50% reduction in calibration time while maintaining estimation accuracy.
item.dc:creator: David Shnaiderov, Matan Ben Dov, Yoav Woldiger, Assaf Hamo, Eugene Demler, Emanuele G. Dalla Torre

item.title: Learning to stabilize nonequilibrium phases of matter with active feedback using partial information
item.description: arXiv:2508.06612v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in quantum computing experiments have enabled new pathways for feedback control. Here, we investigate the role of information in interactive quantum many-body dynamics to engineer out-of-equilibrium phases of matter. To this end, we train reinforcement learning agents to prevent entanglement spreading in (1+1)-dimensional stabilizer circuits with up to 128 qubits. We find that, above an information threshold, agents learn stochastic near-optimal strategies that prevent the system from reaching volume-law entangled states and instead stabilize area-law scaling. These strategies rely on bottlenecks that divide the system and cap the entanglement in the steady state. Crucially, learned strategies are inherently out of equilibrium, require real-time active feedback, and could not be reproduced by simple human-designed control rules. This work establishes the foundations for information-driven individual control of many interacting quantum degrees of freedom, demonstrating the capabilities of reinforcement learning to stabilize and uncover novel critical properties of many-body nonequilibrium steady states.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Cemin, Markus Schmitt, Marin Bukov

item.title: Global Clock-Based Stochastic Modeling of a Memory-Assisted Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution System
item.description: arXiv:2508.14983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On the pathway to quantum key distribution on a global scale will be the realization of metropolitan-sized, Memory-Assisted Measurement-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (MA-MDI-QKD) systems. Here, we present a simplistic and intuitive stochastic model to predict error-corrected key throughput in a MA-MDI-QKD scheme that incorporates a series of channel and quantum memory parameters. Building on our recently introduced global and local clock framework for entanglement distribution, our model employs a global clock system that accounts for the asynchronous arrival of Alice and Bob's qubits at the central station through leveraging quantum memories. By focusing on metropolitan distances, we predict an error-corrected throughput metric over ranges of 10-50 km. Our streamlined approach is a valuable addition to existing quantum network simulators that will guide the smooth integration of quantum networking into the field of communications engineering.
item.dc:creator: Fares Nada, Amber Hussain, Tasmi R. Ahmed, Andrew MacRae, Connor Kupchak

item.title: Quantum algorithms for Uhlmann transformation
item.description: arXiv:2509.03619v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Uhlmann's theorem is a central result in quantum information theory, which associates the closeness of two quantum states with that of their purifications. This theorem characterizes a fundamental task: transforming one quantum state into another via local operations acting only on a subsystem. The optimal transformation for this task is called the Uhlmann transformation, which has applications in various information-processing tasks. However, its quantum circuit implementation and computational cost have remained unclear, limiting its utility. In this work, we fill this gap by proposing quantum algorithms that realize the Uhlmann transformation in query and sample access models. Our algorithms in the purified access models can be implemented in polynomial time for low-rank states, exhibiting an exponential improvement over the prior approach and other naive approaches based on quantum state tomography. We also derive lower bounds on the query and sample costs of the Uhlmann transformation, thereby revealing the computational limits for this task. In the purified access models, these bounds match the costs of our algorithms up to logarithmic factors in terms of the rank, the accuracy, and the minimum non-zero singular value associated with the fidelity. In the mixed sample access model with the canonical purification, our algorithm attains the optimal scaling in the dimension and the accuracy. We apply our Uhlmann transformation algorithms to the fidelity estimation problem and substantially improve the previous best query and sample costs, where our costs attain the optimal scaling in the rank, and the sample cost also in the accuracy. We further discuss other applications to information-theoretic tasks, including quantum communication, quantum state merging, and the algorithmic implementation of the Petz recovery map, providing a comprehensive evaluation of their computational costs.
item.dc:creator: Takeru Utsumi, Yoshifumi Nakata, Qisheng Wang, Ryuji Takagi

item.title: Probabilistic perfect pure quantum state transfer via state restoring and ancilla measurement
item.description: arXiv:2509.10100v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose the protocol for the probabilistic perfect state transfer of an arbitrary multiqubit pure quantum state along the spin-1/2 chain governed by the Hamiltonian preserving the excitation number in the system. We show that the multiqubit $k$-excitation pure sender's state can be restored at the receiver using only the local transformations over the qubits of the extended receiver. The restored state appears in the superposition with other states which form garbage. This garbage can be easily removed by including the ancilla, whose state labels the garbage, and then measuring the ancilla state with desired output. The resulting state of the receiver coincides with the initial sender's state. Then, to transfer an arbitrary multiqubit pure state of some system $S^{(0)}$, we encode this state into the $k$-excitation state of the sender, transfer and restore this state and finally decode the restored $k$-excitation state of the receiver into the state of another subsystem $R^{(0)}$. After labeling and removing the garbage via the ancilla-state measuring with certain success probability we complete the algorithm for the probabilistic perfect transfer of an arbitrary pure state.
item.dc:creator: E. B. Fel'dman, J. Wu, A. I. Zenchuk

item.title: Adversarial Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2510.08298v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In thermodynamics, an agent's ability to extract work is fundamentally constrained by their environment. Traditional frameworks struggle to capture how strategic decision-making under uncertainty, particularly an agent's tolerance for risk, determines the trade-off between extractable work and probability of success in finite-scale experiments. Here, we develop a framework for nonequilibrium thermodynamics based on adversarial resource theories, in which work extraction is modeled as an adversarial game for an agent extracting work. Within this perspective, we consider a Szilard-type engine as a game isomorphic to Kelly gambling, an information-theoretic model of optimal betting under uncertainty -- but with a thermodynamic utility function. Extending the framework to finite-size regimes, we apply a risk-reward trade-off to find an interpretation of the Renyi divergences in terms of extractable work for a given failure probability. By incorporating risk sensitivity via utility functions, we show that the guaranteed amount of work a rational agent would accept instead of undertaking a risky protocol is given by a Renyi divergence. This provides a unified picture of thermodynamics and gambling, and highlights how generalized free energies emerge from an adversarial setup.
item.dc:creator: Maite Arcos, Philippe Faist, Takahiro Sagawa, Jonathan Oppenheim

item.title: Globalizing the Carleman linear embedding method for nonlinear dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2510.15715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Carleman embedding method is a well-known technique for linearizing a system of nonlinear differential equations, but fails to converge in regions where there are multiple fixed points. We prove that the need for the solution to be expressible as a convergent Taylor series of the initial conditions leads to restrictions on the stability and convergence of the Carleman algorithm. Inspired by this realization, we propose and test three different versions of a global piecewise Carleman embedding technique, based on partitioning space into multiple regions where the center and size of the embedding region are chosen to control convergence. The first method switches between local linearization regions of fixed size once the trajectory reaches the boundary of the current linearization chart. During the transition, the embedding is reconstructed within the newly created chart, centered at the transition point. The second method also adapts the chart size dynamically, enhancing accuracy in regions where multiple fixed points are located. The third method partitions the state space using a static grid with precomputed linearization charts of fixed size, making it more suitable for applications that require high speed. All techniques are numerically tested on multiple integrable and chaotic nonlinear dynamical systems demonstrating their applicability for problems that are completely intractable for the standard Carleman embedding method. Simulations of chaotic dynamical systems such as various types of strange attractors demonstrate the power of the adaptive methods. However, global Carleman methods face fundamental limitations when simulating chaotic nonlinear systems on quantum computers due to overhead during nonlinear remapping.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Novikau, Ilon Joseph

item.title: Hybridized-Mode Parametric Amplifier in Kinetic-Inductance Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2512.03362v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parametric amplification is essential for quantum measurement, enabling the amplification of weak microwave signals with minimal added noise. While Josephson-junction-based amplifiers have become standard in superconducting quantum circuits, their magnetic sensitivity, limited saturation power, and sub-kelvin operating requirements motivate the development of alternative nonlinear platforms. Here we demonstrate a two-mode kinetic-inductance parametric amplifier based on a pair of capacitively coupled Kerr-nonlinear resonators fabricated from NbTiN and NbN thin films. The distributed Kerr nonlinearity of these materials enables nondegenerate four-wave-mixing amplification with gains approaching 40 dB, gain-bandwidth products up to 6.9 MHz, and 1-dB compression powers two to three orders of magnitude higher than those of state-of-the-art Josephson amplifiers. A coupled-mode theoretical model accurately captures the pump-induced modification of the hybridized modes and quantitatively reproduces the observed signal and idler responses. The NbN device exhibits a significantly larger Kerr coefficient and superior gain-bandwidth performance, highlighting the advantages of high-kinetic-inductance materials. Our results establish coupled kinetic-inductance resonators as a robust platform for broadband, high-power, and magnetically resilient quantum-limited amplification, offering a scalable route for advanced readout in superconducting qubits, spin ensembles, quantum dots, and other microwave-quantum technologies.
item.dc:creator: Danial Davoudi, Abdul Mohamed, Shabir Barzanjeh

item.title: QuantGraph: A Receding-Horizon Quantum Graph Solver
item.description: arXiv:2512.15476v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dynamic programming is a cornerstone of graph-based optimization. While effective, it scales unfavorably with problem size. In this work, we present QuantGraph, a two-stage quantum-enhanced framework that casts local and global graph-optimization problems as quantum-searches over discrete trajectory spaces. The solver is designed to operate efficiently by first finding a sequence of locally optimal transitions in the graph (local stage), without considering full trajectories. The accumulated cost of the resulting candidate acts as a threshold that prunes the search space (up to 60% reduction for certain examples). The subsequent global stage, based on this threshold, refines the solution. To achieve scalability and robustness, we draw on principles from control theory and embed QuantGraph's global stage within a receding-horizon model-predictive-control scheme. This classical layer stabilizes and guides the quantum search, improving precision and reducing computational burden. In practice, the resulting closed-loop system exhibits robust behavior and lower query complexity. Notably, for a fixed control horizon and query budget, QuantGraph supports approximately twice as many control discretization bits while still benefiting from Grover-search's inherent quadratic speedup compared to classical methods.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Vaidhyanathan, Aristotelis Papatheodorou, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur, Mark T. Mitchison, Natalia Ares, Ioannis Havoutis

item.title: Single-LED-pumped, room-temperature, solid-state maser
item.description: arXiv:2512.20611v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optically-pumped, solid-state (OPSS) masers show promise as quantum sensors, oscillators, and amplifiers -even when operating at room temperature. Here we show that the brightness (i.e., the luminance emitted at the surface) of a light-emitting diode (LED) is sufficient to pump such a maser above threshold. Specifically, we demonstrate pulsed maser oscillation in a microwave cavity at room temperature containing a crystal of pentacene-doped para-terphenyl (ptc:ptp) pumped by a single, commercial, chip-scale LED emitting green-yellow light. The LED is driven by discharging a physically small, low-voltage capacitor, resulting in a bench-top maser that is more compact, and a good deal cheaper to make, than existing embodiments. The ptc:ptp crystal is pumped invasively through a fused-quartz waveguide whose outputting facets are shaped like the tip of a spear. An alternative butt-coupled geometry was also tried but failed to mase. Towards explaining our results, the established mean-field formula for a maser's cooperativity is extended to account for a spatially varying optical pump intensity (thus excitation rate) across a spatially varying a.c. magnetic field B(r) (of the cavity's TE_01delta maser mode). This extension leads to a dimensionless figure of merit, we call the ``strike fraction'' (appearing as a factor in the cooperativity), that quantifies how well the applied optical pump targets those regions of the maser crystal where B(r) is strongest. We go on to show how, provided the spatial profile of B(r) is known (through electromagnetic FEM-based simulation), the strike fraction can be straightforwardedly estimated, via Monte Carlo integration, from the data set of an optical ray-tracing simulation of the pump light. These developments allow a Tavis-Cummings-like model (master equation), encompassing terms up to 2nd-order in quantum cumulants, to simulate the process of masing.
item.dc:creator: Michael Newns, Shirley Xu, Mingyang Liu, Yifan Yu, Zike Cheng, Vanessa Ussalim, Zitong Qin, Ziqiu Huang, Max Attwood, Mark Oxborrow

item.title: Reversing Heat Flow by Coherence in a Multipartite Quantum System
item.description: arXiv:2601.00198v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The second law of thermodynamics dictates that heat flows spontaneously from a high-temperature entity to a lower-temperature one. Yet, recent advances have demonstrated that quantum correlations between a system and its thermal environment can induce a reversal of heat flow, challenging classical thermodynamic expectations. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that internal quantum coherence in a multipartite spin system can also reverse heat flow, without relying on correlations with the environment. Under the collision model with cascade interaction, we verify that both the strength and the phase of the coherence term determine the direction and magnitude of energy transfer.These results enable precise control of heat flow using only local quantum properties.
item.dc:creator: Keyi Huang, Qi Zhang, Xiangjing Liu, Ruiqing Li, Xinyue Long, Hongfeng Liu, Xiangyu Wang, Yu-ang Fan, Yuxuan Zheng, Yufang Feng, Yu Zhou, Jack Ng, Xinfang Nie, Zhong-Xiao Man, Dawei Lu

item.title: Stochastic phase-space simulation of multimode cat states via the positive-P representation
item.description: arXiv:2601.07049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a comprehensive study of the transient dynamics of multimode Schr\"odinger cat states in dissipatively coupled resonator arrays using the positive-P phase-space method. By employing the positive-P representation, we derive the exact stochastic differential equations governing the system's dynamics, enabling the simulation of system sizes significantly larger than those accessible via direct master equation simulation. We demonstrate the utility of this method by simulating transient dynamics for networks up to N=21 sites. Furthermore, we critically examine the method's usefulness and limitations, specifically highlighting the computational instability encountered when estimating the state parity in the systems. Our results provide a pathway for scalable simulations of non-Gaussian states in large open quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Yi Shi, Alex Ferrier, Piotr Deuar, Eran Ginossar, Marzena Szymanska

item.title: A Generalized Landauer's Principle for Unitarily Transformed Thermal Reservoirs
item.description: arXiv:2602.04552v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Landauer's principle, a cornerstone of quantum information and thermodynamics, appears to be violated when the thermal reservoir is replaced by a squeezed thermal state (STS), owing to the additional thermodynamic resources inherently present in the squeezed state. We introduce a formal extension of the principle to such unitarily transformed thermal states. By defining an effective Hamiltonian, we rigorously establish a generalized Landauer inequality, which naturally reduces to the standard case for an ordinary thermal reservoir as a special instance. The framework further yields a consistent definition of entropy production and a proof of its non-negativity. We illustrate its utility by studying an arbitrarily moving Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to a quantum field initially prepared in the STS. Using perturbation theory, we compute the entropy production explicitly, confirming its positivity. As a result of the symmetry breaking induced by the unitary transformation, it depends on both the proper time interval and the absolute spacetime position. Our work clarifies the apparent violation of Landauer's principle with STSs by providing a consistent information-theoretic framework. It also offers a practical tool for computing entropy production in non-equilibrium and relativistic settings, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines and information protocols.
item.dc:creator: Hao Xu

item.title: Ground state and persistent oscillations in the quantum East model
item.description: arXiv:2602.23422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the 1D quantum East model with open boundary and no global conserved charge, we show that in the limit $s \to -\infty$, the ground state is approximately captured by a simple spin-polarized product state. The polarization angle changes as we approach the quantum phase transition at $s = 0$ where the ground state becomes an exact product state polarized along the X-axis. For $s \to -\infty$, we further identify a low-entanglement excited eigenstate that differs from the ground state only by a $\pi$-rotation of the first spin and is well approximated by a spin-coherent state. For $-1\lesssim s<0$, this spin-coherent state overlaps mainly with two eigenstates separated by a system size-independent energy gap, leading to long-lived coherent oscillations of local observables near the edge. These oscillations originate from boundary physics and are distinct from quantum many-body scars and hypercube-like Fock-space mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Adway Kumar Das, Achilleas Lazarides

item.title: The stabilizer ground state and applications to quantum simulation
item.description: arXiv:2603.06286v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The stabilizer ground state is the lowest energy stabilizer state with respect to a given Hamiltonian. This is useful in quantum simulation contexts as it allows for a Clifford circuit approximation of a ground state that can be further refined towards the true ground state. However, in many cases it is highly degenerate and does not give a unique stabilizer state. In this paper, we define and investigate methods to prepare the optimal stabilizer ground state (OSGS), which is the stabilizer ground state that has the highest fidelity with the true ground state. We show how the optimal stabilizer ground state may be evaluated by classically selecting the optimal stabilizer group and employing the stabilizer tableaux formalism.We show applications of the OSGS in the context of measurement-based deterministic imaginary time evolution, where it is used as a highly efficient initial state for the evolution towards the true ground state. Candidate commuting subsets are generated from the target Hamiltonian using a genetic search guided by energy evaluations incorporating an inner optimization over generator signs. Once a complete signed generating set is specified, the corresponding state can be efficiently prepared using Clifford gates. Complexity analysis further shows that the algorithm's resource scales polynomially with system dimension, highlighting its efficiency and potential quantum advantage.
item.dc:creator: Yuping Mao, Jiaxing Feng, Yimeng Mao, Tim Byrnes

item.title: Thermalization Across Scales on a Digital Quantum Processor
item.description: arXiv:2603.12236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems normally unfolds via dynamical spreading of entanglement across progressively increasing spatial scales. The speed of this dynamical process, however, can be affected by the presence of local disorder. Here we study the crossover between slow and fast thermalization in a disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg Floquet model using digital quantum simulations with up to 100 superconducting qubits. Our experiment measures subsystem purities and $Z$-basis marginal collision entropies for patches of up to $3\times 3$ qubits. We resolve the onset of thermalization across scales by tracking each quantity's approach to its asymptotic value. In regimes where the system is moderately entangled, we validate our calibrated quantum simulations against state-of-the-art classical simulations. Near the crossover to fast thermalization, the classical methods no longer reliably converge due to volume-law growth of entanglement. By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.By exploring this computationally hard regime, our work establishes a frontier of applications for digital quantum computers in probing complex many-body thermalization.
item.dc:creator: Faisal Alam, Marcos Crichigno, Elizabeth Crosson, Steven T. Flammia, Filippo Maria Gambetta, Max Hunter Gordon, Michael Kreshchuk, Ashley Montanaro, Alberto Nocera, Raul A. Santos

item.title: Experimental realization of a $\cos(2\varphi)$ transmon qubit
item.description: arXiv:2603.13114v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Symmetry-based selection rules make some atomic states remarkably long-lived, a protection superconducting circuits usually lack. We report coherent control and single-shot readout of a 13.6 MHz $\cos 2\varphi$ qubit in the soft-transmon regime. It consists of an island shunted to ground through an interferometer of Josephson junctions and superinductances that favors tunneling of pairs of Cooper pairs, so that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects the qubit from dielectric loss. We measure a qubit charge matrix element over 100 times smaller than that of the circuit's unprotected plasmon transition, placing the dielectric limit on the qubit lifetime above 10 ms. The measured $T_1 = 70\,\mu$s is instead predicted, with no free parameters, by the $1/f$ flux noise in the interferometer loop that limits dephasing ($T_{2\mathrm{E}} = 2.5\,\mu$s). This experiment demonstrates that Cooper-pair parity symmetry protects against the dielectric loss it targets, and that the remaining limit is the interferometer's sensitivity to flux noise, which larger superinductances are predicted to reduce without compromising protection.
item.dc:creator: Erwan Roverc'h, Alvise Borgognoni, Marius Villiers, Kyrylo Gerashchenko, W. Clarke Smith, Christopher Wilson, Benoit Dou\c{c}ot, Alexandru Petrescu, Philippe Campagne-Ibarcq, Zaki Leghtas

item.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
item.description: arXiv:2603.16765v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.
item.dc:creator: Eric J. Sung, Charles A. Stafford

item.title: Nonperturbative Resummation of Divergent Time-Local Generators: Disentangling Non-Markovian Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2603.25512v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Perturbative van Kampen cumulant expansions of time-local generators of open quantum systems generically diverge at long times, while the reduced dynamics remains regular. We show that these divergences encode information sufficient to reconstruct an approximate nonperturbative dynamical map. Although their resummation remains divergent, disentangling the dynamics according to its van Hove limit resolves the divergence and exposes its dynamical origin: the map approaches isolated times at which it becomes noninvertible. For the weak-coupling unbiased spin--boson model, the reconstructed non-Markovian dynamics takes the disentangled form \begin{equation*} \Phi=\Phi_{\mathrm{GAD}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{NS}}+\Phi_{\mathrm{Khal}}, \end{equation*} separating generalized amplitude damping, exponentially damped nonsecular coherence mixing, and a projective, phase-selective Khalfin map. Thus, the onset of recurrent noninvertibility is the reduced-dynamical-map manifestation of the Khalfin transition from exponential to algebraic relaxation. Although the coherences acquire algebraic Khalfin tails, the distinguishability of quantum superposition states remains governed by an exponential decay law well after the Khalfin transition. Comparison with numerically exact TEMPO dynamics validates the procedure and shows that apparently complex non-Markovian dynamics can resolve into a small number of distinct, physically transparent dynamical processes.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Davidovic 2026 J. Phys. A: Math. Theor.
item.dc:creator: Dragomir Davidovic

item.title: Adaptive Negativity Estimation via Collective Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2603.25560v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper explores an efficient method for entanglement quantification in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit quantum systems based upon the framework of collective measurements in conjunction with machine learning. We introduce an adaptive measurement procedure in which measurement settings are dynamically adjusted based on prior measurement outcomes aiming to optimize the inference precision given a limited number of these measurement settings. The procedure makes use of the Long Short-Term Memory networks to recurrently process collective measurements on two copies of the investigated states. Obtained results demonstrate the tangible benefits of the adaptive measurements in comparison to previously described non-adaptive strategies.
item.dc:creator: Martin Zeman, Vojt\v{e}ch Tr\'avn\'i\v{c}ek, Anton\'in \v{C}ernoch, Jan Soubusta, Karel Lemr

item.title: Quantum metrological advantage of high-order squeezed states
item.description: arXiv:2604.09958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum correlations can be harnessed to improve the precision in parameter estimation beyond classical capabilities. Under a standard interferometric or rotation protocol, it is well established that the optimal single-mode Gaussian state is a standard squeezed vacuum, which enables Heisenberg-limited precision. In this work, we investigate the potential metrological advantage of two distinct families involving high-order squeezing, namely, mth-phase and multisqueezed states. Our results show that these non-Gaussian states can grant a significant metrological advantage with respect to the optimal squeezed vacuum under equivalent conditions, i.e., at equal occupations. Their advantage holds at both low and large occupations, but its behavior critically depends on the chosen family of high-order squeezing. While higher squeezing orders enhance the advantage, this comes at the cost of higher-order observables in the measurement for full metrological performance. Finally, we study their robustness to standard decoherence channels, i.e., pure dephasing and zero-temperature damping. Employing standard squeezing as reference state, our results indicate a reasonable robustness against damping up to a certain noise strength, while their metrological advantage becomes fragile under pure dephasing. Our work shows the potential enhancement in quantum metrology beyond Gaussian states, carefully detailing the main challenges and limitations.
item.dc:creator: Rub\'en Gordillo-Hachuel, Erik Torrontegui, Cristina de Dios, Ricardo Puebla

item.title: Spectrum analysis with quantum dynamical systems. II. Finite-time analysis
item.description: arXiv:2604.11614v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The prequel to this work [Ng et al., Phys. Rev. A 93, 042121 (2016)] proposes the method of spectral photon counting to enhance noise spectroscopy with an optical interferometer. While the predicted enhancement over homodyne detection is promising, the results there are derived by taking an asymptotic limit of infinite observation time; their validity for a finite time remains unclear. To validate the theory, here we perform a numerical study of a finite-time model. Assuming that the signal is an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process with an unknown variance parameter, we evaluate the Fisher information for homodyne detection, a lower bound on the Fisher information for spectral photon counting, and a quantum upper bound, all without taking the infinite-time limit. To confirm that the Fisher-information quantities are satisfactory precision measures, we also compute the errors of the maximum-likelihood estimator by Monte-Carlo simulations. The results demonstrate that the Fisher-information quantities and the estimation errors all smoothly approach their asymptotic limits, and the advantage of spectral photon counting over homodyne detection can remain substantial for finite times.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Sui, Mankei Tsang

item.title: What Can Actually Be Proved About the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Paradox? Operational Consistency, Locality, and Quantum Completeness
item.description: arXiv:2604.13135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) argument concerns whether accurate quantum predictions imply a complete description of physical reality. We distinguish predictive adequacy, operational no-signalling, EPR elements of reality, and ontological completeness. We formalize the EPR reality criterion using observable-, value-, and context-dependent predicates and prove that its incompleteness implication does not entail a prohibition on objectively stochastic origins of outcomes. A two-observable stochastic-source countermodel establishes this limited logical non-entailment, without addressing randomness generated at measurement or reproducing the full quantum assemblage. We illustrate the latter distinction using an established two-setting qubit steering inequality. For continuous variables, we derive inferred-variance and Gaussian-steering criteria for a stipulated instantaneous elastic-collision map, studying mass ratios, incident wave-packet spreading, covariance inflation, and readout noise. We distinguish losses of fixed-axis Reid violations from losses of optimized Gaussian steering. These results are conditional benchmarks, not predictions for the proposed finite-duration ion-collision apparatus, whose scattering dynamics and preparation and measurement parameters remain unspecified. We also show why uncertainty inequalities and exponential decay memorylessness alone do not establish intrinsic ontological randomness. The analysis delimits the logical and physical assumptions needed for claims about EPR completeness without proposing a new hidden-variable dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Miko{\l}aj Sienicki, Krzysztof Sienicki

item.title: Cloning is as Hard as Learning for Stabilizer States
item.description: arXiv:2604.15269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The impossibility of simultaneously cloning non-orthogonal states lies at the foundations of quantum theory. Even when allowing for approximation errors, cloning an arbitrary unknown pure state requires as many initial copies as needed to fully learn the state. Rather than arbitrary unknown states, modern quantum learning theory often considers structured classes of states and exploits such structure to develop learning algorithms that outperform general-state tomography. This raises the question: How do the sample complexities of learning and cloning relate for such structured classes. We answer this question for an important class of states. Namely, for $n$-qubit stabilizer states, we show that the optimal sample complexity of cloning is $\Theta(n)$. Thus, also for this structured class of states, cloning is as hard as learning. To prove this result, we relate stabilizer state cloning to a variant of the sample amplification problem for probability distributions that was recently introduced in classical learning theory. This allows us to obtain our cloning lower bounds in analogy to new sample amplification lower bounds for classes of distributions with an underlying linear structure. Our results provide a more fine-grained perspective on No-Cloning theorems, opening up connections from foundations to quantum learning theory and quantum cryptography.
item.dc:creator: Nikhil Bansal, Matthias C. Caro, Gaurav Mahajan

item.title: Tuning of quantum nanoscaled friction within the Prandtl-Tomlinson model
item.description: arXiv:2604.27216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nanoscaled is a fundamental tribological phenomenon with complex behavior of its dynamical force. Here, we utilize the Prandtl-Tomlinson framework to investigate systematically the different means of control of the frictional force at the quantum and classical levels. It is found that the frictional dynamics can be controlled by the corrugation and characteristic length ratio parameters dependent upon properties of the nanoparticle-chain system. In addition to the stick-slip regime, other types of motion are uncovered, highlighting the richness of the frictional dynamics. The importance of Landau-Zener tunneling for the quantum motion is also analyzed. These findings provide valuable insights for interpreting experimental observations and controlling quantum frictional behavior in nanoscale systems.
item.dc:creator: Dai-Nam Le, Lilia M. Woods

item.title: Weak ergodicity breaking captured from short-time dynamcis and graph theory
item.description: arXiv:2605.00094v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the onset of weak ergodicity violations in closed quantum many-body systems and focus on cases in which they occur through a transition that is controlled by a model parameter, a scenario called a weak ergodicity-breaking transition. This situation is realized in the Rosenzweig-Porter model and the quantum sun model, which we investigate here. Our analysis is based on representing quantum systems in Fock space and examining the short-time dynamics of density autocorrelation functions. From these, we extract proxies for decay rates for each individual basis state. As a first main result, we show that the distribution of such decay rates captures known weak ergodicity-breaking transitions in both models. As a second main result, we establish a connection between the decay rates of density autocorrelations and graph-theoretical measures. Concretely, we demonstrate that moments of the distribution of the recently introduced graph-energy centrality also detect the weak ergodicity transitions, which is inherited from the behavior of the decay rates. While most numerical tools are limited to small system sizes, the quantities studied in our work can be calculated analytically for large systems of many hundreds of sites and in some cases, even in the thermodynamic limit.
item.dc:creator: Heiko Georg Menzler, Rafa{\l} \'Swi\k{e}tek, Mari Carmen Ba\~nuls, Fabian Heidrich-Meisner

item.title: Angular-momentum quantization as intrinsic reference for complete RF polarimetry with Rydberg atoms
item.description: arXiv:2605.14529v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rydberg electrometry leverages non-metallic vapor cells with highly excited atoms to link RF field properties to a spectroscopic readout in the optical domain. Demonstrations have so far mainly addressed linearly polarized fields inducing a rotationally invariant atomic dressed-level splitting. Here we report on measurements of RF fields in a general state of polarization (SOP) which we map onto the Poincar\'e sphere through spectroscopic fingerprints characteristic of a member of an angular-momentum hierarchy. For SOPs circumnavigating the Poincar\'e sphere's prime meridian, we witness a continuous transformation of the member's eigenenergy spectrum. Conversely, such fingerprints can be used as input to a protocol for polarimetric characterization of the RF field, and we demonstrate its extension to SOPs beyond the prime meridian. Because the relative positions of eigenenergies are locked in place by angular-momentum quantization, the framework is universal and calibration-free, and our specific demonstration in rubidium generalizes to all systems with a single valence electron.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Chilcott, Laurits N. Stokholm, Matthew Cloutman, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, Niels Kj{\ae}rgaard

item.title: Wave packet landscape in open quantum systems
item.description: arXiv:2605.15658v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate a landscape theory for the long-time wave packet spreading of free and harmonically trapped particles with quantum fluctuations and its related dissipation. We show that the diffusion, localization, and collapse of wave packets arise from symmetry structures of an underlying landscape in covariance space. The geometry of this landscape determines the asymptotic fate of the wave packet. In the quantum landscape description, the trapping potential and bath fluctuation break the landscape symmetry in distinct ways: the former lifts the valley-like landscape of a fluctuation-free free particle into a bowl-like landscape, leading to collapse, whereas the latter tilts the valley and turns localization into diffusion. The resulting landscape symmetry breaking accounts for the noncommuting long-time limits and abrupt changes in the asymptotic wave-packet width. This establishes landscape symmetry breaking as a unified geometric origin of wave-packet diffusion, localization, and collapse in quantum Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: Kang Xu, Miao-Miao Yi, Zi-Hong Yan, C. P. Sun

item.title: A reason why we do not observe Schr\"odinger's cats
item.description: arXiv:2605.16148v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A reason is discussed (may be not the only one) for why we do not see any superposition of macroscopic states in the real world. Under the general assumption that quantum macrostates are statistical ensembles of microstates, it is shown that any superposition of macrostates is reduced in a very short time by the unitary dynamics of the ordinary Schr\"odinger equation, deducing the Born rule without having to postulate it. In more detail, the macroscopic and microscopic degrees of freedom are decoupled in the Schr\"odinger equation, yielding an effective stochastic equation for the macroscopic variables, with the ensemble average of the microscopic amplitudes that acts as a self-generated internal white noise. The stochastic equation is shown to be a reducing It\^o equation if some general causality conditions are met, predicting a very quick collapse of any macroscopic superposition upon formation, with probabilities which satisfy the Born rule. In the context of the von Neumann measurement scheme, the relevance of the result is discussed as a simple dynamical solution of the measurement problem.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Siringo

item.title: Identifiability and endpoint reconstruction of time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from projective trajectory jets
item.description: arXiv:2605.22796v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the identifiability of smooth time-dependent Jacobi Hamiltonians from phase-resolved Schrodinger trajectories. When the initial state is localized at a chain endpoint, we prove that the projective trajectory jet through order M+1 uniquely determines the first M couplings, their logarithmic time derivatives, and the associated diagonal energy differences at preparation. This derivative order is necessary in the unrestricted real-Jacobi class. If only the first K projective coordinates are observed, even their full Taylor jets leave every deeper instantaneous layer undetermined. We also construct evolutions that are indistinguishable on an observation window separated from preparation but have different endpoint coupling scales and rates. We identify two ways to restore local identifiability: first-order projective and reference-population data at generic times, or second-order data from ceil(M/2) suitable site preparations for independent coupling rates. Statistical distinguishability bounds and finite-window simulations quantify the effects of noise, nuisance coefficients, and acquisition design.
item.dc:creator: A. M. Tishin

item.title: Subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures in the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces in the quantum-computing speedup theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.03859v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The quantum-computing speedup theory considers the symmetric structures and properties of quantum systems as the fundamental Quantum-Computing-Speedup (QCS) resources which are responsible for exponentially speeding up quantum computing and simulating. At present a large and important problem is how to make use of the fundamental QCS resources to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. Here the author makes a great effort toward solving this important problem. The theoretical research work in this paper is mainly divided into the two Parts I and II. The Part I investigates mainly the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces. And the relationships are analyzed among the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, quantum simulating for the unitary time-evolutional processes, and the fundamental QCS resources which exist in the different kinds of basic quantum spaces: the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, the density operator spaces, and the Hilbert spaces. It concludes that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space must be positioned as the central place where the fundamental QCS resources are exploited to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. The Part II investigates mainly the subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures. Recognize that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space is the central place. Then those fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space (a quantum-state space) must be explicitly taken into account in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space (a linear operator space). This is an important problem. The subspace-selective unitary manipulation is able to solve this problem. It aims to harness the fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space to speed up quantum computing and simulating in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space.
item.dc:creator: Xijia Miao

item.title: Measuring Entanglement in Qubit System
item.description: arXiv:2606.05056v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An operational way of measuring entanglement in a balanced two-path interferometers is presented, where path information is carried by some internal degree of freedom which, in turn, gets entangled with an ancilla system. The analysis is based on a tripartite description involving paths, an internal qubit degree of freedom, and some ancillary states entangled with the internal degree of freedom. It is then applied to two physically distinct experimental situations: a modified Stern-Gerlach interferometer with spin-1/2 particles and a Mach-Zehnder interferometer with photons carrying polarization. The ancilla degree of freedom may not be experimentally accessible. Tracing out the ancillary system, and employing a quantum erasing procedure based on the internal degree of freedom, it is demonstrated that a concurrence-based measure of the entanglement, between the internal degree of freedom and the ancilla, can be extracted directly from measurable asymmetry of the two output channels. These results show that loss of coherence, quantum erasure, and entanglement estimation in interferometric experiments arise from the same underlying correlation structure and provide a compact experimentally accessible framework for quantifying entanglement in qubit systems.
item.dc:creator: Vignesh S, Tabish Qureshi

item.title: Quantum Correlation Hierarchy and Teleportation in Dephased Hydrogen Hyperfine System
item.description: arXiv:2606.11731v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the dynamics of quantum correlations in the hydrogen hyperfine spin system subject to Markovian phase noise. Treating the electron and proton spin degrees of freedom as an open two-qubit system governed by an isotropic hyperfine Hamiltonian and local dephasing, we obtain the exact time-dependent density matrix and derive analytical expressions for the full X-state family. We compute concurrence($C$), trace-distance measurement-induced nonlocality (Trace MIN--$\mathcal{N}_1$), and average steering coherence (ASC) in closed form and establish their strict ordering $ C(t)\leq \mathcal{N}_1(t)\leq \mathrm{ASC}(t) $ at all times. Entanglement is identified as the most fragile resource, undergoing sudden death at a finite time. Trace MIN exhibits dephasing-immune freezing for states with nonzero population imbalance, while ASC is the most robust quantity, persisting longest in every scenario studied.We additionally demonstrate that the dephased thermal hyperfine state serves as a resource for quantum teleportation, deriving a closed-form expression for the average fidelity and establishing that the teleportation advantage window coincides exactly with the entanglement survival interval, $\mathcal{F}_A > 2/3 \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{C} > 0$, for the full X-state family with maximally mixed marginals. We identify four distinct dynamical regimes and map all three correlation measures onto directly measurable Pauli spin correlators, enabling experimental reconstruction of the full hierarchy without full state tomography.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications (2026), Article 132167
item.dc:creator: Geerthana Thiyagarajan, R. Muthuganesan

item.title: Broadband High-Level Squeezed Light using Waveguide Optical Parametric Amplifiers with External Dispersion Compensation
item.description: arXiv:2606.17422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate broadband phase-sensitive amplification (PSA) measurement of squeezed light generated by a waveguide optical parametric amplifier (OPA) with external dispersion compensation. In broadband systems, group velocity dispersion (GVD) induces a frequency-dependent rotation of the squeezing axis, which limits the observable bandwidth in PSA measurements. While dispersion compensation between two OPAs has been demonstrated previously, we show that the quantity to be compensated is not the material group-delay dispersion $D$ itself but a gain-dependent effective value $D\tanh r/(2r)$, where $r$ is the squeezing parameter, and realize the compensation with free-space fused-silica plates whose insertion loss is $0.4\%$. As a result, we observe a maximum squeezing of $5.9\pm0.2$~dB near the carrier frequency and more than 5~dB of squeezing up to a frequency offset of $5.9\pm0.1$ THz from the carrier. Furthermore, squeezing below the shot-noise level is confirmed up to a frequency offset of $6.9\pm0.1$ THz from the carrier, corresponding to the accessible phase-matching bandwidth of the waveguide OPA. Our results establish a practical method for broadband characterization of squeezed light and provide a key step toward ultrafast continuous-variable quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: Takumi Suzuki, Shotaro Oki, Kazuki Hirota, Takaya Hoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Takahiro Kashiwazaki, Taichi Yamashima, Asuka Inoue, Takeshi Umeki, Mamoru Endo, Akira Furusawa

item.title: Quantum Beam-Splitter Cooling and Thermometry in Large Trapped-Ion Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2606.21357v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose and characterize a protocol for rapid near-ground state cooling of the center-of-mass (c.m.) mode of a large trapped ion crystal. When the initial mean thermal occupation of the mode $\bar{n}_i$ is small compared to the number of ions $N$ ($\bar{n}_i \ll N$), a red sideband drive implements a beam-splitter type state exchange (SWAP operation) between the mode and the collective spin of the $N$ ions, with the latter effectively serving as a quantum harmonic oscillator. Subsequently, a reset of the spins removes the entropy, leading to near-ground state cooling of the c.m. mode. We term this protocol as quantum beam-splitter cooling (QBSC). We analyze the impact of several practical imperfections on the final temperature achievable under QBSC, including finite ion number, off-resonant carrier and blue-sideband contributions, the sideband drives arising from spectator modes, and spatially inhomogeneous driving across the crystal. We outline practical strategies to eliminate the carrier drive. We extend our analysis to multiple cycles of QBSC and also generalize the analysis to demonstrate the cooling of non-c.m. modes using this protocol. Furthermore, we show that measuring the population statistics of the ions at the end of the SWAP operation can enable near-optimal quantum beam-splitter thermometry (QBST), with the classical Fisher information approaching the quantum Fisher information of a thermal state. We discuss the connection of QBSC with continuous sideband cooling and compare QBST with a recently proposed rapid adiabatic passage-based thermometry scheme. Our work constitutes an example of harnessing many-body effects to open new routes to laser cooling and thermometry in large trapped ion crystals.
item.dc:creator: Kirthik Rajakumar, Ansh Das, Abhinay Pandey, Athreya Shankar

item.title: A Universal Telecom-Band Quantum Memory Enabled by Cross-Phase Modulation
item.description: arXiv:2606.24681v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum memories capable of storing and retrieving photonic quantum states on demand are essential for quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and the synchronization of probabilistic quantum processes. All-optical loop-based memories offer broadband operation and compatibility with telecommunication infrastructure, but their performance is often limited by switching losses and the noise introduced by active control mechanisms. Here, we demonstrate a universal all-fiber quantum memory based on two Sagnac interferometers acting as dynamically controlled mirrors through cross-phase modulation. This all-optical switching mechanism enables an input/output transmission as high as 90% (0.46 dB insertion loss), a round-trip transmission of 94.6%, and a characteristic storage lifetime of $18.54 \pm 0.21 \mu s$. The memory exhibits an operational spectral range exceeding 12.5 THz, while keeping noise to negligible levels across the whole telecom C-band. We experimentally demonstrate the preservation of time-bin-encoded heralded photons and time-bin entanglement, as well as compatibility with polarization- and frequency-bin-encoded optical states. Furthermore, we demonstrate the simultaneous storage of over 200 temporal modes and the selective retrieval of independently addressable modes.
